verses.text: Two full years passed. Then Pharaoh dreamed he was standing beside the Nile. 🌙
In the dream, seven healthy, fat cows came up from the river and grazed in the reeds. 🐄
Then seven more cows came up after them—ugly and thin—and stood by the first cows at the riverbank. 🐄
The ugly, skinny cows ate the seven healthy ones. Pharaoh woke up. 😨
He fell asleep again and dreamed a second time. Seven full, healthy heads of grain grew on one stalk. 🌾
After them, seven thin heads of grain sprouted, scorched by the east wind. 🌬️
The thin heads swallowed the seven full ones. Pharaoh woke up and realized it had all been a dream. 😳
When morning came, Pharaoh was deeply troubled. He called Egypt’s magicians and wise men and told them his dreams, but nobody could explain them. 🧙
Then the chief cupbearer told Pharaoh, “Today I remember what I did wrong. 🙋
“Pharaoh was angry with his servants and locked me up with the chief baker in the captain of the guard’s house. ⛓️
“One night, he and I each had a dream, and each dream had its own meaning. 🌙
“A young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams, and he explained each one. 🗣️
“Things happened exactly as he said: I got my position back, and the baker was hanged.” 📜
Pharaoh sent for Joseph, and they hurried him out of the dungeon. Joseph shaved, changed clothes, and came before Pharaoh. 🏃
Pharaoh said, “I had a dream, and nobody can explain it. I’ve heard that when you hear a dream, you can interpret it.” 👑
Joseph answered, “That ability isn’t mine. God will give Pharaoh a peaceful answer.” 🙏
Pharaoh told him, “In my dream, I was standing on the riverbank. 🌊
“Seven healthy, fat cows came up from the river and grazed in the reeds. 🐄
“Then seven more came after them—so thin and ugly, I’d never seen their like anywhere in Egypt. 😟
“The thin, ugly cows ate the first seven fat cows. 🐄
“After they ate them, you couldn’t even tell they’d eaten anything. They still looked just as ugly as before. Then I woke up. 😳
“I dreamed again: seven full, healthy heads of grain grew on one stalk. 🌾
“After them came seven thin, withered heads of grain, scorched by the east wind. 🌬️
“The thin heads swallowed the seven good ones. I told the magicians, but nobody could explain it to me.” 🤷
Joseph told Pharaoh, “Both dreams mean the same thing. God is showing Pharaoh what He is about to do. 📖
“The seven healthy cows mean seven years, and the seven good heads of grain mean seven years too. It’s one message. 7️⃣🌾
“The seven thin, ugly cows that came after them—and the seven empty heads scorched by the east wind—mean seven years of famine. ⚠️
“That’s what I told Pharaoh: God has shown you what He is about to do. 📖
“Seven years of great plenty are coming across all Egypt. 🌾
“After that, seven years of famine will come. People will forget the abundance, and famine will consume the land. 🥀
“The plenty will be forgotten because the famine that follows will be so severe. ⚠️
“Pharaoh had the same dream twice because God has firmly decided this and will bring it about soon.” ⏳
“So Pharaoh should choose a discerning, wise man and put him in charge of Egypt. 🧠
“Pharaoh should appoint overseers across the land and collect one fifth of Egypt’s harvest during the seven good years. 📊
“Have them gather all the food from these good years and store the grain in Pharaoh’s cities, under his authority. 🏙️
“That food will keep the land supplied through the seven famine years, so the country won’t be wiped out by hunger.” 🛟
Pharaoh and all his servants agreed that Joseph’s plan was good. ✅
Pharaoh asked his servants, “Can we find anyone like this—a man with the Spirit of God in him?” 🙏
Then Pharaoh told Joseph, “Since God has shown you all this, nobody is as discerning and wise as you. 👑
“You’ll be in charge of my household, and all my people will follow your word. Only the throne will rank above you.” 🔑
Pharaoh told Joseph, “See, I’m putting you in charge of all Egypt.” 👑
Pharaoh took his signet ring off and put it on Joseph’s hand. He dressed him in fine linen and placed a gold chain around his neck. 💍
He had Joseph ride in his second chariot, and people called out, “Bow the knee!” Pharaoh put him over all Egypt. 🐎
Pharaoh told Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but nobody in all Egypt will lift a hand or foot without your say-so.” 🏛️
Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-Paneah and gave him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, as his wife. Joseph went out across Egypt. 📜
Joseph was thirty when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Then he left Pharaoh’s court and traveled throughout Egypt. 🧭
During the seven years of plenty, the land produced harvest after abundant harvest. 🌾
Joseph gathered food from those seven years and stored it in the cities. In each city, he stored the food grown in the surrounding fields. 🏙️
Joseph stored grain like the sand by the sea—so much that he finally stopped counting. It was beyond measure. 🌊
Before the famine began, Joseph and Asenath—daughter of Potiphera, priest of On—had two sons. 👶
Joseph named his firstborn Manasseh, saying, “God has helped me forget my hardship and all my father’s household.” 💭
He named his second son Ephraim, saying, “God has made me fruitful in this land where I suffered.” 🌱
The seven years of plenty in Egypt came to an end. ⏳
Then the seven famine years began, just as Joseph had said. Other lands faced famine, but Egypt had food. ⚠️
When hunger spread through Egypt, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh told the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. Do whatever he tells you.” 🍞
The famine had spread across the whole land. Joseph opened the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in Egypt. 🏚️
People came to Egypt from every country to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine was severe everywhere. 🌍
